artifact: BBMA cross-module typed-reference identity and mutation inventory

method.function_parser: Balanced-brace source parser with comments and string literals masked; parsed user-function calls were cross-checked against the accepted current-source overlay.
method.parameter_scope: Call sites passing a struct-typed parameter declared by reference (&), including nested member paths, across module boundaries.
method.identity_resolution: Context-insensitive propagation through by-reference function parameters to direct global roots or function-local objects/copies.
method.write_effect_scope: Direct parameter assignments plus transitive propagation through user-defined struct-reference calls; this is a static subset and does not infer all external builtin or global side effects.

root_kind_definition.global-subobject: Argument names a global struct object or nested member directly.
root_kind_definition.forwarded-reference: Argument is a by-reference caller parameter forwarded unchanged.
root_kind_definition.member-of-reference-param: Argument is a nested member rooted in a by-reference caller parameter.
root_kind_definition.local-object: Argument is a function-local struct object.
root_kind_definition.local-copy: Argument is a function-local struct value initialized from another expression; identity is distinct from its source.
root_kind_definition.global-object: Argument is a global struct object without a member path.
root_kind_definition.value-param-copy: Argument is a by-value parameter copy.

limitations: Multiple resolved origins for one source call site indicate context alternatives; the inventory is context-insensitive and does not bind runtime call order or index values.
It does not model function pointers, pointer arithmetic, all MQL builtins that mutate references/arrays, or direct global side effects not expressed through the tracked parameter.
No dependency absence is inferred. Runtime behavior, compiler acceptance, tester behavior, and broker behavior are not certified.
